choices.english: Its encircling walls are walls of fire
rejected: Its flames are flames of fire
choices.why: Cyril reads περίπτερα as the structure round a building and glosses it as the walls of the Church; 'flames' would break the link to his gloss

choices.english: Baal-hamon means 'among those who have believed'
choices.why: plain English; the name is given in its usual English spelling

choices.term: Ἀξιοῖ δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκβαλεῖν ... ἐπὶ τοὺς ἁγίους ἐλθεῖν
choices.english: She also asks Him to cast out the wicked ... she asks Him to come to the saints
rejected: so as to come to the saints
choices.why: both infinitives depend on ἀξιοῖ, so these are two requests, not a purpose clause

choices.english: the burial that Joseph and Nicodemus provided
choices.why: 'provided' fits a burial in English; the note records the literal 'brought'

pass_a_gloss: [Finding] you. That is, outside Jerusalem where He was crucified. Or the burial he says, which brought Joseph and Nicodemus. Pomegranates he says, of the saints. Her wings, wings of fire. The walls, he says, of the Church are fire. To the spiritual Solomon a vineyard came to be; he says the Church. The Beelamon is interpreted 'Among those who have believed'. Who have believed, or [rather] those who received His commandments? The one sitting in gardens oversees the Churches; the companions attend, nor do they judge, but all the judgment the Son does. The bride desires to hear: Enter into the joy of your Lord. She asks Him also the wicked to cast out, Flee, saying, upon the saints to come.
pass_b_english: 'Finding you' (Song of Songs 8:1): that is, outside Jerusalem, where He was crucified (Hebrews 13:12). Or he means the burial that Joseph and Nicodemus provided (John 19:38–40). By pomegranates (Song of Songs 8:2) he means the saints. 'Its encircling walls are walls of fire' (Song of Songs 8:6): the walls of the Church, he says, are fire.

The spiritual Solomon came to have a vineyard (Song of Songs 8:11), and he means the Church. Baal-hamon means 'among those who have believed'. And who are the ones who have believed, if not those who received His commandments?

The one who sits in the gardens (Song of Songs 8:13) watches over the Churches. The companions listen, and they do not judge; rather, the Son does all the judging (John 5:22). The bride longs to hear, 'Enter into the joy of your Lord' (Matthew 25:21). She also asks Him to cast out the wicked, and by saying 'Flee' (Song of Songs 8:14) she asks Him to come to the saints.
source_text:
σε. Ἤγουν ἔξω Ἱερουσαλὴμ ὅπου ἐσταυρώθη. Ἢ τὸν ἐνταφιασμὸν λέγει, ὃν ἤνεγκεν
Ἰωσὴφ καὶ Νικόδημος. Ῥοῶν δὲ λέγει τῶν ἁγίων. Περίπτερα αὐτῆς, περίπτερα
πυρός. Τὰ τείχη, φησὶν, τῆς Ἐκκλησίας πῦρ ἐστι.
Τῷ πνευματικῷ Σαλομὼν ἀμπελὼν ἐγενήθη· λέγει δὲ τὴν Ἐκκλησίαν. Τὸ δὲ
Βεελαμὼν Ἐν τοῖς πεπιστευκόσιν ἑρμηνεύεται. Τίνες δὲ πεπιστεύκασιν, ἢ οἱ τὰς
ἐντολὰς αὐτοῦ δεξάμενοι; Ὁ μὲν καθήμενος ἐν κήποις, τὰς Ἐκκλησίας ἐπισκοπεῖ· οἱ
ἑταῖροι δὲ προσέχουσιν, οὐδὲ κρίνου 69.1293 σιν, ἀλλὰ τὴν κρίσιν πᾶσαν ὁ Υἱὸς
ποιεῖ. Ἐπιθυμεῖ δὲ ἡ νύμφη ἀκοῦσαι· Εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ Κυρίου σου. Ἀξιοῖ δὲ
αὐτὸν καὶ τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκβαλεῖν, Φύγε, λέγουσα, ἐπὶ τοὺς ἁγίους ἐλθεῖν.

5

notes: Source checked clause by clause against PG 69 col. 1292-1293.
The lemma 'Εὑροῦσά σε' (Song of Songs 8:1) is split across the row break; both words are translated here.
The PG column number '69.1293' inside 'κρίνουσιν' and the stray '5' at the end of the row are print furniture and are not translated.
Song of Songs 8:14 bids the beloved flee upon the mountains of spices; Cyril reads those mountains as the saints.
The lemma 'Εὑροῦσά σε' ('finding you', Song of Songs 8:1 LXX: 'finding you outside, I would kiss you') is split across the row break; both words are translated here.
'Or he means the burial that Joseph and Nicodemus provided': ἤνεγκεν, literally 'brought', recalls the myrrh and aloes Nicodemus brought and the linen Joseph supplied (John 19:38–40).
'Ῥοῶν δὲ λέγει τῶν ἁγίων' glosses 'the juice of my pomegranates' (Song of Songs 8:2 LXX).

'Περίπτερα αὐτῆς, περίπτερα πυρός' follows the LXX of Song of Songs 8:6 (English 'its flashes are flashes of fire'). Cyril takes περίπτερα in its architectural sense, the structure that runs round a building, which is why he glosses it as the walls of the Church; it is rendered 'encircling walls' so the gloss makes sense.
'Βεελαμών' is the LXX form of Baal-hamon (Song of Songs 8:11); the name is given in its usual English spelling.
'τὴν κρίσιν πᾶσαν ὁ Υἱὸς ποιεῖ' recalls John 5:22, 'the Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son'.
'Enter into the joy of your Lord' is Matthew 25:21 (repeated in 25:23).

'Ἀξιοῖ δὲ αὐτὸν καὶ τοὺς πονηροὺς ἐκβαλεῖν, Φύγε, λέγουσα, ἐπὶ τοὺς ἁγίους ἐλθεῖν': both infinitives depend on ἀξιοῖ, so she asks Him to cast out the wicked and to come to the saints. Song of Songs 8:14 bids the beloved flee 'upon the mountains of spices'; Cyril reads those mountains as the saints.
The stray '5' at the end of the source row is a page or column number from the print and is not translated.
